coursesExamined.name: Personal & Professional Development
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops academic writing and research-literacy skills alongside personal development and civic engagement. Students locate and evaluate scholarly sources, synthesize literature, formulate research questions and arguments, and construct a research-paper introduction. A community-engaged project with a societal partner connects these skills to collaboration, reflection and practical contribution. Personal development planning addresses learning goals, self-efficacy, and stress and time management; the course also considers responsible academic use of AI.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.
coursesExamined.contribution: Required personal and academic development, research literacy and civic engagement.

coursesExamined.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces financial accounting, management accounting and investment appraisal, including accounting's social role and accountability implications. Students record transactions, prepare and interpret financial statements, and analyze performance and financing. The course then examines costing, pricing, budgeting, organizational control and sustainable management accounting. Investment decisions are evaluated using accounting and discounted-cash-flow measures. A case study analyzes the misuse of an accounting principle and its financial-statement effects.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops financial and management accounting,financial-statement interpretation,costing,budgeting and discounted-cash-flow investment appraisal. It directly supports corporate financial decisions,without providing a complete specialist financial-economics sequence.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements. Students learn how to comprehend a typical corporate annual report and to use accounting as a tool in understanding how economic events affect business.

coursesExamined.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. AI foundations and limitations lead into applications across enterprise functions and industries, labour-market change, productivity, innovation, market structure and inequality. Governance, corporate responsibility, regulation and future scenarios connect technological developments to institutional choices. Students analyze business cases and competing scholarly arguments, then investigate a country's AI readiness, workforce, regulation and industrial policy.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course includes a multi-faceted exploration of AI’s business, managerial, economic and related societal implications. Designed for students with a strong interest in AI, it requires no prior technical background.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines the economic and managerial consequences of AI and technological change
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Examines AI's business, economic and societal implications without requiring a technical background. Students study AI's capabilities and limits, applications across business functions and industries, and effects on labour markets, productivity, innovation and inequality. Business cases and scholarly arguments support analysis of governance, regulation and a country's AI readiness and industrial policy.

coursesExamined.name: Money, Banking & Finance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines financial markets and institutions, including the pricing of bonds, stocks and derivatives, interest rates and their risk and term structure, commercial-bank balance sheets and performance, financial structure and regulation, banking fragility and financial crises, central banks, money creation and monetary policy. Students apply algebraic and graphical analysis to financial and monetary problems. In the Stanford Banking Game they manage a simulated bank, analyse performance in Excel dashboards, forecast financial statements, and make evidence-based decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk. A small research project extends a selected financial or monetary research article through additional literature, a case study or updated evidence.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: We study financial markets (stocks, bonds, derivatives) and financial institutions (commercial banks and central banks). We address such questions as: Can you outperform the stock market? Why are banks inherently fragile? What do central banks do? What causes financial crises? Throughout the semester, student teams participate in a business simulation, the Stanford Banking Game. Each team manages a virtual bank and tries to maximize its share price.
coursesExamined.contribution: Direct securities/bond/stock/derivative pricing,interest-rate risk andtermstructure,bank balance-sheet/capital/liquidity/risk decisions,monetarypolicy andfinancialcrises. Excel-basedbankmanagementsimulation and research-articleextension add substantivefinancialanalysis,not merely budgeting.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Examines financial markets, commercial banks and central banks, including interest rates, financial regulation, financial crises and monetary policy. Students analyse financial problems and manage a simulated bank in the Stanford Banking Game, using Excel dashboards and financial forecasts to inform decisions about loans, deposits, capital, liquidity and risk.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces microeconomic principles and short-run macroeconomic analysis. The microeconomic component examines supply and demand, strategic interaction, consumer choice, production, costs and competitive markets. The macroeconomic component introduces output, unemployment and inflation, then relates goods and financial markets through the IS-LM model. Students use algebra and graphs to explain economic behaviour and apply models to economic issues.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides foundational microeconomic and macroeconomic analysis of markets, firms, households and the wider economy
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions. This course introduces key concepts from both microeconomics and macroeconomics, including markets, incentives, and the principles of supply and demand, and provides a foundation for analyzing real-world economic issues.

coursesExamined.name: International Macroeconomics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.
coursesExamined.contribution: Develops macroeconomic short/medium/long-run models,expectations,open-economy andfiscal/monetary policy using algebra,graphs andindicators; no unverified dedicatedtrade-theory sequence asserted.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends.

coursesExamined.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops microeconomic theory through consumer behaviour, imperfectly competitive markets and economy-wide allocation. Students examine choice under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations, then monopoly, strategic behaviour and labour and capital markets. General equilibrium, efficiency, externalities and government complete the analysis. Algebraic problem-solving and graphical analysis are connected to the interpretation and evaluation of research papers.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity. Explore key concepts such as rational choice, decision-making under uncertainty, and non-egoistic preferences. Analyze market structures, strategic interactions, and factor markets. Learn how markets function and examine the impact of regulation. Develop analytical tools to better understand behavior and engage with empirical research.
coursesExamined.contribution: develops advanced microeconomic analysis of choice under uncertainty, firms and markets

coursesExamined.name: Public Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.
coursesExamined.contribution: examines market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, redistribution and government intervention
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare.

coursesExamined.name: Econometrics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

coursesExamined.name: Behavioral Economics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

coursesExamined.name: Consumer Product Design
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Teaches consumer-product design and development through projects that progress from understanding an existing product to creating a new one. Students investigate product mechanisms and environmental impact, interview potential customers, translate needs into specifications, select concepts, and develop production plans and prototypes where feasible. The final project integrates these stages with industrial scaling and elementary economic analysis. Sustainability, including material use, repairability, lifespan and circularity, informs design decisions throughout.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. We go through the phases of design and development: probe customer needs, translate these into a product concept, develop a fabrication method, analyze sustainability, analyze costs and proceeds. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
coursesExamined.contribution: Specific complementary product-development work translates customer needs into design, production, cost/proceeds and sustainability decisions. It is not an additional economics theory course.

Students will explore real-life case studies, develop a strategic marketing plan and learn how marketers build sustainable brand strategies.

coursesExamined.name: International Business & Governance
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines how international trade, globalization and political, sociocultural and technological forces shape firms' cross-border decisions. Economic foundations include trade theories, foreign direct investment, foreign exchange and the monetary system. Students analyze governance, responsibility and trade-policy conflicts, investigate an international-business question, and develop an evidence-based market-entry strategy covering country attractiveness and business functions. A tariff case applies game theory to stakeholder choices and negotiation.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses. It first explores how international companies operate, then centers on key global challenges including cross-border governance, corporate responsibility, geopolitical strategies and global trade. It provides a comprehensive understanding of today’s complex international business environment.

coursesExamined.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces entrepreneurship and core business functions through the development of a startup concept. Students use design thinking to discover customer needs, define a problem, generate and prototype solutions, and construct value propositions and business models. Marketing, finance, operations, human resources and funding inform a coherent business plan and investor pitch. Entrepreneurial cases and a startup simulation examine decision-making, early growth and business lifecycles, with attention to societal impact and sustainability.

No prior business expertise is required as teams work on a startup project from ideation to final pitch while gaining business and entrepreneurial skills in areas such as design thinking, business model and customer validation. The class fosters creativity and collaboration to drive business and social innovation.

coursesExamined.name: Research Methods & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project. Students study operationalization, measurement quality, sampling, surveys and experimental and nonexperimental designs, then descriptive statistics, estimation, hypothesis testing and introductory regression. R and R Commander support data display and analysis. Project teams develop instruments and a research plan, collect and analyze data, and report results under explicit research-ethics and privacy requirements.

You’ll learn how to plan research logically, from designing studies to working with real data using experimental and survey techniques. You’ll also study descriptive and inferential statistics, with a brief intro to multivariate tools.

coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines organizational behaviour at individual, group and organizational levels. Workshops develop literature searching, study selection, source appraisal and synthesis, linking organizational-psychology evidence to practical questions and recommendations.

coursesExamined.name: Decision-making in AI
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops the mathematical foundations of intelligent-agent decisions under uncertainty. Probability and Bayesian networks support belief updating and inference, while temporal models address changing environments. Decision theory, Markov decision processes, partial observability and bandit problems connect uncertainty to policies and expected utility. Multi-agent decisions introduce strategic and collective interaction, and probabilistic programming provides a framework for expressing models. Students work through equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces planning techniques for AI systems in deterministic and non‑deterministic environments. Addresses uncertainty, partial observability, resource planning and optimizing behaviour under constraints.
coursesExamined.contribution: Probability,Bayesian inference,expectedutility,temporalmodels,Markovdecisionprocesses andbandits develop formal decisions underuncertainty,complementing financialrisk/economicchoice; intelligentagent rather than finance setting.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Decision-making in AI examines how intelligent agents make decisions under uncertainty. Multi-agent decisions and probabilistic programming extend the analysis, supported by equations, numerical examples and scientific papers.

coursesExamined.name: Computational & Numerical Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops numerical solutions to mathematical problems that lack convenient analytical solutions, emphasizing when algorithms work and how to validate their output. Students study numerical root finding, interpolation, differentiation, quadrature, ordinary differential equations, and linear and nonlinear systems. Mathematica notebooks apply and compare textbook algorithms with built-in routines, with attention to roundoff, convergence, error, stability and sensitivity.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations. Emphasises algorithm accuracy, stability and efficiency and uses computer algebra software.

coursesExamined.name: Probability & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference. Students study estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests and maximum-likelihood methods, followed by an introduction to Bayesian reasoning. Mathematica simulations verify analytical results. A substantial project implements and compares random-sampling algorithms, including inverse sampling, accept-reject sampling and Gibbs sampling.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics. Covers probability theory, discrete and continuous distributions, sampling, parameter estimation and simulation; uses computer algebra software to develop theoretical understanding and practical skills.

coursesExamined.name: Ethics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Studies moral reasoning through historical and contemporary ethical theories and close philosophical reading. Utilitarianism, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, virtue ethics, contractarianism and feminist ethics lead into Nietzsche's genealogy, Murdoch's account of goodness and Nagel's treatments of value, perspective, death and meaning. Reflection and research essays require interpretation, argument evaluation and an independent position on ethical theory or a practical ethical problem.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure. coursesExamined.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces epidemiological reasoning and its application to public health. Students measure and interpret disease patterns, study research designs, association, bias, confounding and causality, then examine health determinants, promotion, needs assessment and screening. A local project analyzes a Zeeland health challenge, compares population data, considers affected groups and interventions, and incorporates stakeholder perspectives into feasible recommendations.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead:
Public health is about changing the world. From pandemics to lifestyle-related diseases, from screening for disease to improving water and air quality, it asks: how can we improve to keep the population healthy?_x000D_
But how do we know what actually works? In this course you will dive into epidemiology: the science behind public health. You will learn how to study disease, risks, and changes over time, and how to critically evaluate evidence. Because behind every public health decision lies a question of evidence, and by the end of this course, you will be equipped to engage with it. This course invites you to look beyond the lab, the hospital, and the library, into the wider world where health is shaped. What matters most if we truly care about health, and how can we influence that?
coursesExamined.contribution: introduces epidemiological study design, population health, disease risk and evidence for public-health decisions
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Introduces epidemiology and the evidence used in public health. It examines disease patterns, risks and changes over time, and how research can inform decisions about population health.

coursesExamined.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes. Students study neural signalling, brain anatomy and development, learning, intelligence, personality, social influence, mental disorders and treatments. Several sessions introduce behavioural, imaging and electrophysiological approaches to neuroscience and their combined use. Interdisciplinary research-article and case analysis connects psychological processes to neural mechanisms and clinical questions.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Explores why people behave as they do and how brain injuries affect mental processes. Discusses nature and nurture, introduces brain anatomy and psychological theories, and provides a gateway to cognitive science and clinical psychology.
coursesExamined.contribution: Direct psychological and neuroscientific foundations of behaviour and mental processes, plus methods and brain-function knowledge needed for health psychology. Neural content is complementary to economic decision inquiry, not economic theory.

coursesExamined.name: Social Psychology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Introduces the scientific study of how thoughts, feelings and behaviour are shaped by other people and social situations. Social cognition, the self, influence and persuasion lead into group processes, prejudice, aggression, prosocial behaviour, attraction and close relationships. Students critically examine empirical research, synthesize findings from journal articles, formulate theory-guided questions and design a feasible study. The final project proposes research rather than conducting an empirical investigation.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Covers main theories, findings and principles of social psychology, emphasising its scientific approach to understanding how people’s feelings, thoughts and behaviour are influenced by the presence of others.
coursesExamined.contribution: provides social-psychological analysis of attitudes, influence and group behaviour relevant to consumer and economic choices

coursesExamined.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Develops experimental-design knowledge and practical statistical analysis for health and behavioural research. Students choose, fit, diagnose and interpret multivariable models, comparing means, analyzing categorical outcomes and studying latent constructs. R, primarily through R Commander, supports repeated practical exercises; SPSS is an optional alternative. Data-analysis papers and a poster connect research questions and hypotheses to appropriate models, assumption checks, substantive interpretation and APA reporting.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: The course is necessary for students who want to pursue master programs in psychology and adjacent disciplines, as well as research masters in the medical domain. It is highly recommended also for all those who want to be researchers in other domains. In addition to technical training, the course emphasizes clear academic communication. It will equip you with the skills necessary to apply advanced statistical techniques to real-world research problems. With a focus on practical application through case studies and data analysis projects, You will be able to choose the appropriate statistical model for various research scenarios and address common challenges in data interpretation.

coursesExamined.name: Medical & Health Psychology
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Examines health and illness through interactions among biological, psychological and sociocultural factors. Health inequalities, behaviour and prevention lead into stress, symptoms, pain, medical consultation and treatment decisions. Chronic illness is considered from patients', families' and healthcare professionals' perspectives. Students analyze research, interventions and clinical cases, practice interviewing with attention to culture, and apply clinical-health formulation to understand support and quality of life in medical settings.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: Uses a biopsychosocial approach to explore how biological, psychological and socio‑cultural factors influence health and illness. Covers theories, research and interventions and focuses on the role of psychological expertise in medical settings.
coursesExamined.contribution: Direct study of biopsychosocial determinants of health, stress, illness and health behaviour; a specific complementary health-domain contribution, not economic evaluation of healthcare.

coursesExamined.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Teaches systematic review and meta-analysis for synthesizing evidence in medical, behavioural and related research. Students define review questions, search and select studies, extract and code findings, assess bias and compute effect sizes. Hands-on R work fits fixed- and random-effects models, examines heterogeneity and moderators, conducts meta-regression and investigates publication bias. A group project completes a small meta-analysis and presents its methods and results in a research poster.
coursesExamined.officialDescriptionRead: This course guides you through combining results from multiple studies using systematic reviews and meta-analysis a method now essential in psychology, medicine, social science and other disciplines. Want to know what really works? Gain hands-on skills in research synthesis that inform evidence-based policy and practice. You’ll search literature, manage data, and present findings that matter. Learn to calculate effect sizes, synthesize results and assess bias using R.
coursesExamined.contribution: Direct systematic review and meta-analysis with effect sizes and hands-on R supports evidence synthesis about behaviour and health and evidence-based policy. It is not a substitute for econometric impact evaluation.
coursesExamined.descriptionRead: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics introduces systematic reviews and meta-analysis to synthesise results across studies. Students use R to conduct analyses, work with data structures and packages, estimate treatment effects and examine their consistency across studies. Presentations and active research tasks develop evidence-synthesis skills.

academicJudgment: All three concepts respond to the verified economic/business field and specific formal bachelor-major interests. The broad business option contains substantial economic theory, business decisions, marketing, organisational behaviour, financial accounting/banking and empirical methods. The health option retains economic theory and econometrics, while social/health psychology,population-health assessment,negotiation and systematic review/meta-analysis implement health/consumer decisions. Neuroscience is complementary psychological mechanism study,not a finance or healthcare-economics substitute. The new third puts linear algebra,numerical approximation,programming,probabilistic decisions,optimisation and algorithms alongside pricing/bank-risk/investment decisions and econometric empirical research. Its methods are specific complements with documented analytical roles,not presumed finance-specific coursework. This programme implements quantitative economic/financial inquiry,not a full FinancialEconomicsmajor. Existing first option already contains accounting/banking,so distinctness comes from actual mathematical/computational priorities and removal of marketing/product/organisational courses,not merely a finance label. All courses except PPD have concrete direct/complementary roles in trace.
qualitativeDistinctness: The completed UCR curriculum is broader than pure economics: it combines micro- and macroeconomics with accounting, finance, marketing, strategy, organisational study, data science, econometrics and international business.

Compared with the broad economics/business option, six courses change: psychology and brain/behaviour foundations, health psychology, population-health evidence, negotiation and research synthesis replace mathematical probability/calculus, AI-economy study, international business, product development and practical finance. These changes shift academic weight to behaviour, health determinants and evidence synthesis, while retaining a substantial economic and empirical core. Health psychology and epidemiology complement economics; they do not constitute a health-economics specialist sequence.

Replaces broad marketing/product/organisational study with programming, linear algebra, numerical analysis, probabilistic decisions, optimisation and algorithmic models. The financial-accounting/banking and economic core gives these methods an explicit quantitative economic/financial purpose. Unlike the health option, it does not organise inquiry around psychological mechanisms, clinical behaviour or population-health evidence.
